text: Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Mar 18th, 2026 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: A Review: Please take someone else.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Dec 27th, 2025 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: B Review: He was a nice professor. I took him for two semesters. The professor himself is really calm, nice and very helpful. Although you need to do your own code practice for the lab exam. If you know what you are doing then you will be good.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Oct 12th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: A- Review: His lectures are very boring and hard to sit through. Going to class is pointless and a waste of time. The ZyBooks is also a waste of time. Learn on your own with plenty of resources on YouTube and do your own coding problems separate from the labs. I wish he wasn't the only option for this class.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: Oct 12th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: A- Review: His lectures are uninteresting. ZyBooks is easy to get through but you feel like you are wasting your time doing them and they personally didn't help me learn. Most of the learning I did on my own. He will have projects and labs due the week of the exam. If you take him stick to YouTube and practice coding on your own outside of labs.
Course: CSCE 1030 Date: May 15th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: A Review: DO NOT TAKE.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: May 9th, 2025 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: A Review: Going to class is useless. The homework was very helpful for learning content and the exams were similar to labs so know both very well. The exams are weighted heavily with no drops but doing homework, projects, and labs can make up a bad exam grade. Got a 50 on one exam and ended with a 96 in the class.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: May 8th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: B- Review: This professor was terrible and unfortunately the only person teaching both CSCE 1030 and 1040. Lectures were useless to the point where only 9 people out of 80 from the start were left by the end.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: May 8th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: Rather not say Review: Don't take this professor. Exams are much harder than the study material, lectures are stale, and he is never helpful during office hours and will not respond to emails no matter how long you wait for a reply.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: May 8th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: B+ Review: Terrible professor — if you can avoid taking him please look for any other option. Professor Maharjan really does not care if his students learn anything. His lectures are useless. Also he does not round grades even if they are 0.1 away from the next letter grade.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: May 6th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: B Review: His lectures are not helpful, there are no drops for his exams, and what he teaches is not what is tested — he makes exams harder than the material covered.
Course: CSCE 1030 Date: May 3rd, 2025 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 2 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: Lectures and online resources were well organized.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: Feb 6th, 2025 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: F Review: Decent professor, he would sidetrack a lot during lectures which is why I rarely attended them. Always gave clear instructions though.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: Dec 20th, 2024 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: C+ Review: Horrible professor. He pawns everything on his TAs and believes everything they say. TAs in this class were caught helping students use ChatGPT during exams. He accused students of cheating based solely on TA reports. Be cautious.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: Jun 24th, 2024 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: Rather not say Review: Taking this course was the worst mistake. He was terrible and so difficult to work with. He is never in the lab to help so labs were hard to understand. Exams accounted for more than 60% of your grade. If you have a feeling you won't pass drop the class — it is not worth repeating. Please avoid if possible.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: May 8th, 2024 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: F Review: Even if you study a lot outside of class you will still somehow fail. Each test is worth 55% of your grade.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: May 3rd, 2024 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: Classes are not compulsory but if you don't understand anything just go to class. He is knowledgeable but just reads off the slides which is boring. There are no quizzes but homework is heavy. There are three group projects and four exams including the final. Solo learning is required for getting a good grade.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: Apr 28th, 2024 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: C Review: The lectures are very boring and the professor is not friendly. None of the exams are dropped and each exam is worth 15%. I recommend taking this course with a different professor.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: Nov 16th, 2023 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 1 Would Take Again: No Grade: A+ Review: Lectures were extremely boring but he posts the slideshows on Canvas so there is not really much reason to attend. Labs were actually useful but beware the lab exams and projects — they are very heavily weighted and you don't get any drops on them.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: May 14th, 2023 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: Lectures were pretty boring so I didn't attend. Lots of busywork on ZyBooks so I mainly used that to study. Tests weren't too bad and were similar to labs. The class wasn't hard but had a lot of tedious homework. I've heard the teacher is helpful if you email him. Overall an okay experience — you will be perfectly fine as long as you do your work.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: May 10th, 2023 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: Not sure yet Review: Very exam heavy. All homeworks are basically week-long projects you do by yourself. ZyBooks homework is easy just pay attention to the participation. Don't be afraid to ask questions because they will help you. Don't recommend taking this teacher for more complex classes but for the basics he is average.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: Apr 20th, 2023 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: A- Review: Very dull lectures but I think that is just computer science. He speaks really quietly so be sure to sit in the front. A very kind man and easy to get a hold of. The homework is a lot but as long as you don't do it at the last minute you are good. He has also pushed deadlines back by a day to help students.

Course: CSCE 5640 Date: Mar 20th, 2023 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: A- Review: This professor follows his key sheet to validate answers. If your answer is correct and provides a proper solution he still checks his key sheet for exact word matches. Grading feels very rigid and inflexible.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: Jan 17th, 2023 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 1 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A- Review: Reading the ZyBooks is essential. It will help you on the exams a ton which are worth 67% of the grade in total.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: Dec 31st, 2022 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: D Review: Bunch of homework due each week with projects that can take multiple days of work all worth almost nothing. There are four tests including the final worth a total of 70% of your grade. You will not know what you made on any of the tests for several weeks. Don't take this class if possible.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: Dec 16th, 2022 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: B Review: Canvas lab average will be wrong the entire semester until the very end when he combines the grades — your grade will drop significantly so beware. Grades are unreliable all semester. This course is very hard unless you already have experience in CSCE. Final is comprehensive and open book but worth 20%. Projects weigh less than 3% but help a lot. ---
Course: CSCE 4110 Date: May 6th, 2026 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: B+ Review: All bad reviews but one were removed.

Course: CSCE 4110 Date: May 6th, 2026 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: A- Review: I would recommend not taking this professor if possible. The exam reviews were very unhelpful for the actual exams and cheating was allowed multiple times which ruined the class for everyone else.

Course: CSCE 4110 Date: May 6th, 2026 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: A- Review: At first this professor did very well by providing comprehensive exam reviews for the first exam but for both the second and final we did not receive much of a review and both exams were mostly open-ended questions some of which had never been gone over in class and then she told someone that the final would be curved but later went back on that.

Course: CSCE 4110 Date: May 2nd, 2026 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: B Review: Professor Dorri is a great lecturer with clear examples, but be prepared for unannounced quizzes that heavily impact your grade. Study guides are too vague to help with exams. Also, poor handling of cheating led to assigned seating and harder tests for everyone. TAs are hit-or-miss and can be rude or have an ego. Overall good class but minor issues.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Jan 14th, 2026 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: B Review: I wouldn't take her again. She's kind, but Data Structures needs clear, structured teaching and this class didn't provide that. Many lectures felt rushed or confusing, and I relied heavily on YouTube and notes from other sources to understand the material. Expectations and grading could be clearer.
Course: CSCE 5430 Date: Aug 25th, 2025 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A Review: Very caring. Excellent lectures.
Course: CSCE 5430 Date: Jun 17th, 2025 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: Not sure yet Review: Recommended! Clear grading criteria. Inspirational and caring professor.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: May 14th, 2025 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 1 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: Amazing professor and an easy course overall. Lecture attendance isn't required, but extra credit comes from class participation. Weekly recitations have practice problems which are graded. Review slides and practice problems to prepare well for the exam and the quizzes.

Course: CSCE 4110 Date: Apr 17th, 2025 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A Review: Best professor in CS department. Lectures are comprehensive and she moves through material at the perfect pace. Would take again if the opportunity is presented.

Course: CSCE 4110 Date: Jan 16th, 2025 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 2 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: A great professor. She is helpful inside and outside of class. Our class performed poorly on the first midterm, so she sent out a questionnaire asking what she can do to help. Performance increased on subsequent tests, and she offered extra credit opportunities. Make sure to attend lectures, as she gives out in-class assignments. Highly recommend.

Course: CSCE 4110 Date: Dec 10th, 2024 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: Not sure yet Review: One of my favorite professors here. She explains the material very clearly with examples and is happy to help students who don't understand it. The TAs present during lectures were also very helpful when I was confused. Take notes during class and you'll do fine.

Course: CSCE 5400 Date: Dec 10th, 2024 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A Review: I went to her class daily and she gives us many example problems to practice in the class. Classes are very interactive and she gives bonus points if you solve problems on board. Prompt response to emails both by her and her TAs. She is always accessible and ready to help. I would definitely recommend Mrs. Dorri's class.

Course: CSCE 5400 Date: Dec 9th, 2024 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: Excellent class. The best class that I ever took in UNT. TAs especially Pavan was very helpful throughout the course helping us with difficult problems.

Course: CSCE 4110 Date: Dec 9th, 2024 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A Review: Amazing professor, one of the best among UNTs often disappointing CS staff. Has a great lecture and teaching style. The subject material is tough, but she teaches it effectively. Engage with the material — if you actually show up to class, take notes, and do the assignments, the grades will take care of themselves. Took her for both 4110 and 4115.

Course: CSCE 4110 Date: Dec 1st, 2024 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: Great professor and she is very kind. Teaches and shows everything you need. Makes learning algorithms interesting. Attendance isn't taken but there are random class activities that aren't announced on Canvas so attendance is heavily encouraged.
Course: CSCE 5400 Date: Sep 7th, 2024 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: Not sure yet Review: Good class to learn the subject. Extra credit opportunities available.
Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Aug 23rd, 2024 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A Review: She knows her stuff!
Course: CSCE 4110 Date: May 1st, 2024 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: Amazing professor, she knows her materials!
Course: CSCE 4110 Date: Apr 18th, 2024 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: She explains all topics during lecture very well.
Course: CSCE 4110 Date: Apr 11th, 2024 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: Not sure yet Review: Good class. ---
Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Nov 8th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 1 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: Bro taught so well he got fired.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Sep 9th, 2025 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 1 Would Take Again: No Grade: Incomplete Review: You're reading this looking for a reason to take this prof. There are none. Curtis Chambers teaches so poorly that no one knows exactly how to complete assignments. He regularly fails to attend class, and the syllabus is not updated. He is woefully unprofessional and underprepared.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Sep 9th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: A Review: Brilliant lecturer who doesn't even show up to class. Confusing assignments, syllabus doesn't even include exams, doesn't teach anything, way too much reading and work and assignments, and he doesn't even bother to come to class to lecture.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Aug 24th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: Not sure yet Review: Very not beginner-friendly for coders, his labs are very unclear direction-wise, and you are expected to know everything he speaks on. You are expected to fully understand GitHub and have explored every cranny of it for a surprise group project where you have to find partners. As an online student, this was absolutely draining.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Jul 21st, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: C Review: Learned nothing in this class due to the assignments and project due dates being cut in half. This professor did not host any lectures, grade work or assign due dates. Class ended up being taught by the TA. DO NOT ENROLL IN THIS COURSE WITH THIS PROFESSOR. If you have to then make sure to start on the project on day one and ask the TA for help.

Course: CSCE 2100 Date: Jul 7th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: C Review: Avoid this professor at all costs. Online course, couldn't get correspondence from him until half the course was over. Had to contact the Dean to even get due dates that weren't from last semester's class. Doesn't explain anything, no office hours. All around horrendous experience.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Jun 29th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: Not sure yet Review: The worst professor I've ever had. After the first week, it was 2 weeks and 5 days before we heard another word from him, with 0 due dates assigned. There are two very large projects that are intended to be group projects, but he never created groups. Many assignments are clearly ripped from in-person full-term courses and are always vague. AVOID!

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Jun 15th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: A+ Review: Not in communication with TAs, so they grade harshly. Once I needed to contact him but he canceled class for 2 straight weeks, he doesn't check his email, and he wasn't at any of his office hours. His projects are the only hard part of the class, do not procrastinate them. Multiple choice easy, lectures useless, and coding exams have cheatsheet.

Course: CSCE 2100 Date: Jun 15th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 1 Would Take Again: No Grade: A+ Review: Terrible teacher, reads off of zybooks. Class canceled at least 6-7 times. Won't reply to emails. Often not in office hours. He uses one question bank for quizzes and exams, which are almost all of your grade, so that's extremely easy to get an A in. You might not learn anything though.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Jun 2nd, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: C Review: Attendance is mandatory but his lectures are all over the place, he cancelled class a lot and hardly ever responded to emails. You could check the UNT CSCE discord and find more complaints in detail. If you have the opportunity do not take this professor.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: May 26th, 2025 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: A+ Review: Will cancel class 30 mins before lecture so if you commute get ready for some wasted trips. As far as the work goes it's not too bad as long as you stay on top of it and do exactly what he says on the rubric. If code doesn't compile in the exams you will receive a 0 instead of partial credit. These exams were super easy if you can make a cheatsheet.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: May 12th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: B+ Review: Lectures were disorganized, often canceled or poorly communicated, making it hard to learn. Most of my understanding came from online sources. Project 1 had nearly 4 months while Project 2 had only 2 weeks, yet grading was delayed so long it was hard to recall the assignments. Recitations were mandatory but irrelevant to the main lectures.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: May 2nd, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: Not sure yet Review: It's almost the end of the semester and he just hasn't shown up to class in over 2 weeks. He still hasn't announced when the final exam will be taking place and he has no information about it anywhere in Canvas. Believe every bad review you see about him. UNT should be embarrassed to have someone this incompetent and disorganized on their payroll.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Apr 20th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: Not sure yet Review: He doesn't care about his job, it's as simple as that. The semester is almost over and he's canceled almost 50% of classes. He doesn't answer emails. He talks at you about the career field like he knows something but he's just someone that couldn't make it.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Apr 7th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: Not sure yet Review: This is the worst class I've ever taken. It's disorganized, frequently canceled with little notice, and assignments are given last-minute sometimes due on weekends. The professor is outdated and rigid, and the TAs are unhelpful. UNT seriously needs better grad students and teaching staff.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Mar 21st, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: Rather not say Review: This professor is very disorganized, does not teach, and does not explain the assignment or project in full detail. He reads from Zybooks and random questions during his lectures. The TA doesn't know anything about this class and is not very helpful. Mandatory attendance, exams are online.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Mar 20th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: Not sure yet Review: He's probably the worst professor in UNT's computer science department. The class is very disorganized and the lectures are not useful as he reads off of Zybooks or some mediocre PowerPoint. The assignments, exams, and projects require a ton of work and they need to be perfect due to strict grading. His TAs are also clueless and don't help.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Mar 5th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: Not sure yet Review: Every review of this class you read is factual. He deserves a wedgie. A disgrace of a professor.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Feb 25th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: Not sure yet Review: Data structures are hard as it is learning the rest of C and C++. However, the professor is not the best for teaching content. He makes everything a big deal to the point where everything you do wrong is like a felony. Be prepared to use outside resources as he doesn't teach anything and his TAs are bad.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Feb 12th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: B Review: Very unorganized and expects you to already know the material without teaching it. You basically just learn everything off Zybooks and he expects you to show up to his lectures where he just repeats the slides and adds some comments about how in the real world you'll need this or that. Don't take him. ---

Course: CSCE 4902 Date: Jun 7th, 2026 Rating: 4 Difficulty: 2 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: Capstone is a very different experience from most classes so keep that in mind. Overall he seemed fine, though my interaction with him was limited as my group was assigned to work with a TA. Seems good about responding to emails. Canvas announcements were shockingly illiterate, but it was funny at least. Most important thing is finding a good group.

Course: CSCE 1030 Date: May 1st, 2025 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: A Review: Really quiet, even with a microphone I could barely hear him. Group projects and lots of homework. Beware of pop quizzes.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Apr 30th, 2025 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: A+ Review: First professor where I wanted to rip my eyes out. He is very inconsiderate and does not care that you have other classes and other assignments. He will keep piling homework on you until you actually start crying. This is the first professor after 4 years that I actually wanted to drop out of college. Be prepared.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Jan 15th, 2024 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: B- Review: The exams and homework all build on each other and are quite difficult and time consuming. No useful feedback is given which makes it hard to improve.
Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Nov 27th, 2023 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: A Review: Terrible professor and ideologies.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Oct 19th, 2023 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A- Review: Taught the material very well. Class is decided by 3 projects that are outlined and explained very well and 3 tests that are also explained very well ahead of time. During lectures he also gives great life advice on how to make it in the computer science field which was very nice.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Jul 5th, 2023 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: No Grade: B Review: Keathly's teaching style represents the degrading quality of the CS programs at UNT. All or nothing grading. Zero guidance except for old timey anecdotes. Loves to rant about previous students and the ways he failed them. Meanwhile he literally cannot compile his own code in front of us. Yet we get punished if it happens to us during an exam.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: May 16th, 2023 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: He wasn't easy to talk to but answered any questions very well. Taking this class as a freshman is hard because he doesn't leave room for you to adapt to college. He didn't seem to set clear standards for his TAs or communicate with them well. But he was very good at giving you an idea of what a job in programming will be like.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: May 14th, 2023 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 4 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A Review: As someone who returned to university for a second major, the difference between those who perform well in this class and those who don't boils down to mental preparedness for college. Dr. Keathly admittedly doesn't do the best job at helping freshmen adapt but this class is very doable with some studying and occasional office hours.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: May 8th, 2023 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: B+ Review: Although this was an online course, no resources beyond the textbook were provided. Instructions for projects were significantly lacking and homework assignments were extraordinarily lengthy with just a week to complete them. Requests for clarification were often met with one-sentence replies and little elaboration. Thankfully the textbook is sufficient to pass.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Mar 30th, 2023 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A Review: Prof. Keathly is good at explaining the problems you bring up but he isn't very approachable. The projects were difficult but he went over them in lectures. He offers good extra credit but you need to score a minimum of 70 before he applies it. Exams weren't hard though. Only take him if you're decent at coding and willing to put in the effort.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Feb 4th, 2023 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: Drop/Withdrawal Review: If you don't have a coding background or this is your first coding class at UNT don't take it with him. His instructions are unclear as are his lectures. He says he doesn't expect you to know coding but wants to make you fail assignments and labs for anything. Too much work in too little time.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Dec 26th, 2022 Rating: 5 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A Review: Gave excellent career and industry advice. Genuinely cares about the subjects he teaches and creating competent individuals. Hard work wins in this class, don't procrastinate assignments and watch content on what you are learning outside of lectures and you'll be fine. Interacting with him by asking questions will help a ton.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Aug 23rd, 2022 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: B+ Review: Got an 89.9 but he didn't want to round up to a 90. Tough grader with lots of homework and heavy exams.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Oct 29th, 2021 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 2 Would Take Again: No Grade: A Review: Dr. Keathly is a bit sarcastic with a hint of arrogance, like he needs to prove his worth to his freshman students. The material isn't difficult but there is a lot of it. The assignments are repetitive and time consuming without really teaching anything. I would not recommend.

Course: CSCE 3615 Date: May 8th, 2021 Rating: 4 Difficulty: 1 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: Professor did not really teach the class since it was online. However he had a few remote sessions set up to explain the material that was not included in a textbook. Do your assignments and you will pass. Exams are open-notes and open-book. Almost all assignments had confusing instructions so I needed to clarify them with the professor.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: May 3rd, 2021 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 2 Would Take Again: No Grade: A Review: Not a very interesting instructor. Class is pretty basic and you pretty much only need the information presented in the zyBook. Some labs are intentionally significantly more challenging than others so make sure to carve out some time for them. Homeworks are almost all incredibly lengthy but exams are all coding exams except for the final which is multiple choice.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Apr 23rd, 2021 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A Review: Though some people may dislike the way he teaches I found his class to be fine. You don't need to show up to the lectures and they are always recorded. The benefit of showing up is that he has lots of opportunities for questions which can help a lot. Overall he was much more lenient than what others said and his class is easy if you just try.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Apr 15th, 2021 Rating: 3 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: B+ Review: Had him through Zoom, not terrible but not great either. If you watch the YouTube videos he links and know how to Google, the class isn't bad. Be wary of the homework — the first one is easy but the rest are hard so start them at least 1 week before they are due. He lets you look at labs and have one sheet of notes during exams which helps.

Course: CSCE 3615 Date: Apr 1st, 2021 Rating: 4 Difficulty: 2 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A Review: Good class with a bunch of case studies that taught relevant material. Group projects were a bit extensive however alright in the long term.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Mar 1st, 2021 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: Not sure yet Review: Do not take him. He expects you to know everything day one. There is a homework assignment due every month that you constantly need to work on but you also have assignments in the book and a lab every week. He doesn't teach the content at all and if you need help he provides no help.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Jan 26th, 2021 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: Drop/Withdrawal Review: Guy was a horrible teacher. Doesn't teach, just expects you to know how to do everything flawlessly before doing it. He grades harshly. You're only allowed to use the textbook for help or ask a classmate for help. He expects you to code in a vacuum. He is unhelpful in his office hours. Unfortunately the only CSCE 1040 professor.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Jan 26th, 2021 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 5 Would Take Again: No Grade: B+ Review: I created an account just to rate this professor. By far the most disappointing professor I have ever had. I almost changed my major because he made no effort to teach and there are no other teachers for this class. The main difficulty is the workload — zybooks plus one coding assignment a week with a large project every month. Open notes tests but no leniency.

Course: CSCE 1040 Date: Oct 19th, 2020 Rating: 2 Difficulty: 2 Would Take Again: Yes Grade: A+ Review: Definitely one of the most condescending professors I've had. Really contributes to the elitist STEM stereotype. Like everyone else says he knows what he is doing but does not teach it well. I learned all the material through the YouTube videos he links. Not the worst professor ever but completely dispassionate.

Course: CSCE 2110 Date: Aug 23rd, 2020 Rating: 1 Difficulty: 3 Would Take Again: No Grade: Not sure yet Review: Lectures are boring, he barely explains topics, talks nonsense about the topic, and is a tough grader. I would not recommend taking his class. ---

Course Description, Structure, and Objectives
This course covers cybersecurity terminology, principles, and technologies and introduces students to
security issues related to hardware, software, cryptography, and policy to make better, safer decisions.
Topics include cyber threats and vulnerabilities, information security frameworks and policies,
cryptography, penetration testing, and defense in depth. Many of the techniques will be demonstrated
and practiced using a modern programming language. The goal is to develop a foundation for further
study in cybersecurity. This course takes place in-person, and all assignments will be submitted through
Canvas.

Course Outcomes
Course outcomes are measurable achievements to be accomplished by the completion of a course.
These outcomes are evaluated as part of our ABET accreditation process:

1. Describe basic security terminology and concepts as well as analyze security threats, vulnerabilities,
and attacks.
2. Describe the role of computers and networks in a security context.
3. Develop basic organizational security policies.
4. Demonstrate basic principles and concepts of cryptography and general cryptanalysis.
5. Demonstrate various types of penetration testing to measure the security posture.
6. Discuss the legal and ethical issues involved with securing computer systems, networks, and
information.
7. Apply security design principles using a modern programming language to solve various
cybersecurity problems.

Important Notice for F-1 Students taking Distance Education Courses

Federal Regulation
To read detailed Immigration and Customs Enforcement regulations for F-1 students taking
online courses, please go to the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations website. The
specific portion concerning distance education courses is located at Title 8 CFR 214.2
Paragraph (f)(6)(i)(G).
The paragraph reads:
(G) For F-1 students enrolled in classes for credit or classroom hours, no more than the
equivalent of one class or three credits per session, term, semester, trimester, or quarter
may be counted toward the full course of study requirement if the class is taken on-line or
through distance education and does not require the student's physical attendance for
classes, examination or other purposes integral to completion of the class. An on-line or
distance education course is a course that is offered principally through the use of
television, audio, or computer transmission including open broadcast, closed circuit,
cable, microwave, or satellite, audio conferencing, or computer conferencing. If the F-1
student's course of study is in a language study program, no on-line or distance education
classes may be considered to count toward a student's full course of study requirement.

University of North Texas Compliance
To comply with immigration regulations, an F-1 visa holder within the United States may
need to engage in an on-campus experiential component for this course. This component
(which must be approved in advance by the instructor) can include activities such as taking
an on-campus exam, participating in an on-campus lecture or lab activity, or other on-
campus experience integral to the completion of this course.
If such an on-campus activity is required, it is the student’s responsibility to do the
following:
(1) Submit a written request to the instructor for an on-campus experiential component
within one week of the start of the course.

(2) Ensure that the activity on campus takes place and the instructor documents it in
writing with a notice sent to the International Student and Scholar Services Office. ISSS
has a form available that you may use for this purpose.
Because the decision may have serious immigration consequences, if an F-1 student is
unsure about his or her need to participate in an on-campus experiential component for
this course, s/he should contact the UNT International Student and Scholar Services Office
(telephone 940-565-2195 or email internationaladvising@unt.edu) to get clarification
before the one-week deadline.

Use of Student Work
A student owns the copyright for all work (e.g. software, photographs, reports,
presentations, and email postings) he or she creates within a class and the University is not
entitled to use any student work without the student’s permission unless all of the
following criteria are met:
• The work is used only once.
• The work is not used in its entirety.
• Use of the work does not affect any potential profits from the work.
• The student is not identified.
• The work is identified as student work.
If the use of the work does not meet all of the above criteria, then the University office or
department using the work must obtain the student’s written permission.
